newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Refining to fuel Engen yr profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Refining to fuel Engen yr profits.

text.p: Improved refining margins thanks to a weak rand should help Engen Ltd lift year earnings to between 200 and 220 cents from 128 cents last time when it reports on Monday.
Analysts told Reuters the healthy increase in earnings would mainly be due to external factors, although the full benefits of internal restructuring would hopefully also shine through.
Forecasts on year dividends ranged from 90 to 110 cents for the year to August 31 compared to 60 cents last year.
"The fundamentals for a good, healthy turnaround are there," one analyst said.
The weaker rand would have boosted refining margins which had been under pressure in previous years, while throughput at Engen's Durban refinery was reported to have been better this year.
Industry sources said that this would not entirely have offset the pressure on wholesale margins, which has prompted the industry to ask for a three cents a litre increase.

The government has appointed a task team to consider the request along with the whole pricing structure of fuel. Analysts said that any move to grant the increase or deregulate the market would be good news for Engen.
One analyst said that an increase in the wholesale margin should boost earnings in the current year, which he conservatively forecast at 270 cents.
Last year's results were also expected to be boosted by the steady rise in the demand for fuel in South Africa.
Latest figures from the South African Petroleum Industry Association showed that petroleum product sales have risen by more than six percent every quarter this year despite higher gasoline prices.

Production at the refinery was much smoother this year despite a planned four-week maintenance shutdown and brief technical problems in bunker fuel production that have now been ironed out, analysts said.

Because of the pressure on margins in recent years, Engen's "Project Discovery" of the last two years has focused on cost reduction throughout the operation and analysts said the full benefits of this were now expected to have worked their way through the system.

Any benefits from the sale in June of 30 percent of Engen stock to Malaysia's state-owned Petronas were not expected to be reflected in the results to be released on Monday, but could be a factor next year.
Engen shares have climbed sharply this week, fuelled by hopes of good results, the slide in the rand and high oil prices. On Thursday the stock was trading up a further 40 cents at 27.00 rand.
However, some analysts said they would not get very excited about Engen unless the merger with Sasol Ltd, mooted earlier this year, came through.
But one industry source told Reuters that discussions on such a merger were now on hold until Sasol "reaches a better understanding with the oil industry as a whole".
Synthetic fuel producer Sasol has long been at loggerheads with the oil industry because of the state support it receives, which the oil industry says gives it an unfair advantage.
